new_entities.name: Four or more adverse childhood experiences
new_entities.description: A high cumulative burden of adverse childhood experiences, commonly operationalized as four or more ACEs.

new_entities.name: Adult mental health outcomes
aliases: adult depression, anxiety, PTSD and related outcomes
new_entities.description: Major adult mental health outcomes including depression, anxiety, PTSD, suicidality, and related psychopathology.

edges.effect_quant: A high ACE burden is strongly associated with later adult mental ill-health, with the largest pooled effects often seen for PTSD and consistently elevated odds for depression and anxiety.
edges.population: adults with high cumulative childhood adversity, often operationalized as four or more ACEs
edges.mechanism: Repeated childhood adversity can recalibrate stress-response systems, threat processing, attachment patterns, and health behaviors in ways that make later depression, anxiety, trauma symptoms, and suicidality more likely. The dose-response pattern strengthens the case that cumulative burden matters, not just any single event alone.
edges.summary: This is one of the clearer harm clusters in the ACE literature. Large recent meta-analyses show that cumulative childhood adversity substantially raises the odds of adult depression, anxiety, PTSD, and related outcomes, and the prospective evidence suggests that the signal is not just an artifact of cross-sectional recall.
edges.caveats: The brief asks for `aces_4plus`, but many source studies pool across several cumulative-ACE thresholds rather than isolating exactly four exposures. The evidence is still highly relevant because the dose-response pattern consistently shows the heaviest adversity burden as the highest-risk group.
